title.en: Watch the TLS handshake and certificate

why.en: curl -v prints the TLS version, cipher, certificate subject and issuer, then the HTTP exchange.
why.hinglish: curl -v TLS version, cipher, certificate subject aur issuer print karta hai, phir HTTP exchange.

expect.en: Lines like “TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384”, a server certificate with subject and issuer, then the HTTP request and a 200 response. Exact cipher and issuer vary.
expect.hinglish: “TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384” jaisi lines, subject aur issuer wala server certificate, phir HTTP request aur 200 response. Exact cipher aur issuer badal sakte hain.

why.en: The Strict-Transport-Security header is what makes the browser skip plain HTTP.
why.hinglish: Strict-Transport-Security header hi browser ko plain HTTP skip karne par majboor karta hai.

expect.en: Headers including strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000 (the value may differ).
expect.hinglish: Headers mein strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000 (value alag ho sakti hai).

title.en: Find the Client Hello and its SNI
title.hinglish: Client Hello aur uska SNI dhoondo

why.en: The SNI is sent in clear, so Wireshark can show the site name even though the page is encrypted.
why.hinglish: SNI clear mein bheja jaata hai, isliye page encrypted hone ke bawajood Wireshark site ka naam dikha sakta hai.

expect.en: A Client Hello; expand it to see server_name = example.com, supported versions, ALPN and the key share.
expect.hinglish: Ek Client Hello; use expand karke server_name = example.com, supported versions, ALPN aur key share dekho.

why.en: After the handshake, everything is Application Data records of random-looking bytes.
why.hinglish: Handshake ke baad sab kuch random dikhne wale bytes ke Application Data records hain.

expect.en: Application Data packets with no readable HTTP inside, unlike the plain-HTTP lesson.
expect.hinglish: Application Data packets jinke andar padhne layak HTTP nahi hai, plain-HTTP lesson se alag.
